texts: An LV end-systolic dimension over 50 mm is the finding of severe aortic regurgitation here: A.

Chronic severe regurgitation loads the ventricle with volume; an end-systolic dimension above 50 mm (or 25 mm/m2) marks a ventricle that is starting to fail and is an indication for surgery even without symptoms.
The other thresholds are wrong: severe regurgitation has a pressure half-time under 200 ms, a vena contracta over 6 mm and a jet width of 65 percent or more of the outflow tract.
The flow reversal in the descending aorta that marks severe regurgitation is holodiastolic, not systolic.
In the picture, the tape round the engine room reads past 50 even when the room is at its emptiest.
Memory hook: past fifty even when empty.
